Achieving such CFs would require that these plants be near the top of the dispatch list. This report includes a sensitivity analysis on the impact of plant capacity factor on LCOE. The combustion turbines (CTs) used in each of the IGCC and NGCC configurations are manufactured in discrete sizes, with each of the configurations assuming combustion turbine operation at its rated output. While the output of the combustion turbines is consistent between configurations within a technology type, the IGCC cases have net outputs ranging from 499 (Case B5B-Q) to 641 MW (Case B4A). The range in IGCC net output is caused by the significant auxiliary load imposed in the CO capture cases—primarily due to CO compression— 2 2 and the need for steam for CO capture and the water gas shift (WGS) reactions, which reduces 2 steam turbine output. The output in NGCC cases varies from 640 MW (F-frame CT with 95 percent capture) to 992 MW (H-frame CT without capture). The nominal net plant output for all PC plants in this study is 650 MW, which remains consistent with Revision 4 of this report (Fossil Energy Baseline Revision 4 [FEBR4]). Air pollution control devices for all technologies are designed to meet the limits of the February 2013 update to the New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) for sulfur dioxide (SO ), nitrogen 2 oxide (NOx), and particulate matter (PM), and the March 2013 update to the Utility Mercury and Air Toxics Standards (MATS) for mercury (Hg) and hydrochloric acid (HCl). Liquid waste streams are regulated by the November 2015 update to the Effluent Limitation Guidelines (ELG), and all plants in the study are in compliance. For the IGCC cases, hydrogen sulfide (H S) is separated with an acid gas removal (AGR) process 2 and converted to elemental sulfur in a Claus plant with tail gas recycle to limit SO stack 2 emissions; carbonyl sulfide (COS) hydrolysis is employed in non-capture cases, but not in capture cases where WGS is used; NOx formation is minimized with low NOx burners (LNBs) and nitrogen (N ) dilution, and where required, syngas humidification; the PM is controlled with 2 some combination of a water quench, syngas scrubber, cyclone, and/or candle filter, depending on the gasifier technology; Hg is controlled with dual sulfur-impregnated carbon beds; the HCl is primarily removed in the syngas scrubber with the remainder removed with the low temperature heat recovery condensate. The HCl is removed from the syngas scrubber effluent with a brine concentrator and crystallizer.
